When adding allowlist entries or suppressions to secret-scanning or other security-scanning tools, scope them as narrowly as possible so legitimate exceptions (e.g., synthetic test credentials or known-safe identifiers) are ignored without weakening detection of real secrets or vulnerabilities nearby. Prefer precise matching conditions (e.g., combining rule ID, exact regex match, and file path with AND logic) over broad path- or rule-level exclusions. For example, in `.gitleaks.toml`, use a `generic-api-key` rule allowlist with `condition = AND` and `regexTarget = match` to exempt only the specific synthetic model IDs, not the entire file or rule. After adding any such exemption, verify it by testing that the intended values are ignored while an unrelated, genuinely sensitive value in the same file or path is still flagged as a violation.
